title: Flat folding at one vertex
sections: Work locally around one interior vertex of an ideal uncut sheet. Distinct rays bound positive sectors totaling 360°; every listed ray is folded fully flat, with no extra creases. Mountain (M) and valley (V) labels are read from one fixed marked side. Layers may touch but may not pass through one another.

Kawasaki’s angle condition: A single-vertex pattern with unassigned M/V labels is locally flat-foldable exactly when it has an even number of rays and its alternating sector sums are both 180°. The guide develops the necessary orientation/angle obstruction and explicit small constructions; the general converse is cited as adult context.

Maekawa’s condition: In a valid assignment, |M−V|=2, where M and V count the rays of each type. This necessary count, even combined with the angle condition, does not certify an arbitrary prescribed assignment. For the four-right-angle disk, the exact valid assignments are the eight words with three M and one V, or one M and three V. The guide supplies witnesses and a finite layer-order proof.
These are local ideal flat-state statements. They do not prove global flat-foldability of a multi-vertex sheet, specify a rigid-folding motion, or certify that a paper model will collapse easily.
K–1: Refold adult-prepared right-angle models and classify fixed ray labels; no degree arithmetic is needed.
Grades 2–3: Compare loose sector pieces with a half-turn, identify exact mismatches and arrange alternating groups.
Grades 4–5: Explain orientation and alternating-angle necessities; separate obstruction from construction and complete the right-angle classification.

A successful legal fold supplies a witness. Failed attempts alone do not prove impossibility; an exact obstruction does. Repeated trials may suggest a conjecture; angle or layer-order arguments must cover untried cases. No physical folding pretest has been completed for this draft. Before teaching, an adult must try each intended construction with the actual paper, and omit any unready demonstration.
